patterns.name: Primary profile deletion not confirmed
patterns.note: Half of the deletion calls against the account store return FAILED or PARTIAL, so the profile and its secondary identifiers can survive.

patterns.name: Search-index deletion not confirmed
patterns.note: Nine in ten index deletions fail. Index entries are rebuilt from the account store, so they persist and re-appear.

patterns.name: Support redaction and attachment deletion failing
patterns.note: Messages that must be redacted and attachments that must be deleted stay in place for roughly three in four requests.

patterns.name: Export deletion failing
patterns.note: Almost every export deletion fails, leaving downloadable archives of personal data.

patterns.name: Analytics anonymization incomplete
patterns.note: Profiles and telemetry remain attributable to a user in about one case in three.

patterns.name: Replication checkpoint failures
patterns.note: Replica checkpoints fail or stall, which is where rows that no longer exist in the primary come from.

patterns.name: Tombstone redaction failing
patterns.note: Account tombstones keep direct identifiers when the redaction does not finish.

patterns.name: Upstream write failures
patterns.signature: UPDATE / INDEX / SYNC / REFRESH / EMAIL / EXPORT / RETAIN
patterns.note: Partial or failed writes leave copies that disagree with the source, the root cause of most later drift.

patterns.name: Data flow confirmed still enabled
patterns.note: Connector checks that found the flow running. Each one is a path that can copy deleted data back.

patterns.name: Connector repopulated a downstream index
patterns.note: An active connector wrote search entries after the source was handled.

patterns.name: Archive confirmed restorable
patterns.note: Backups that can still be restored. Rule 14 only allows retention when restore access can be blocked.

patterns.name: Completion claimed without a confirmed state
patterns.note: The worker reports completion, or stops on an error, without a final state from the target system. Treat as a claim.

patterns.name: Record written again after a successful delete
patterns.signature: DELETE_RECORD SUCCESS, then a write to the same resource_id
patterns.note: Replication or sync wrote the resource again a median 106 minutes after the delete was reported as done.

patterns.name: Replica holds rows the primary no longer has
patterns.signature: replica table minus primary table, same snapshot
patterns.note: 10 of 14 replica tables in the SQL evidence hold at least one row that is absent from their primary.

register.title: Exports past expiry, last seen downloadable
register.why: The export window has closed (expires_at is before the end of the evidence window), so nothing needs the archive.
register.conflict: Each was still marked download_available at its last snapshot. A link that outlives its expiry keeps a full copy outside any deletion run.
register.action: DELETE_RECORD on the export job and its object

register.title: Archives that can still be restored
register.why: Backups are kept only if restore access can be blocked, and these allow restore.
register.conflict: A restore would bring back profile, search and analytics rows that were already deleted.

register.title: Continuous-sync connectors still enabled
register.why: Once the source record is deleted the connector has no legitimate reason to run.
register.conflict: An enabled connector copies customer events to the warehouse and search again after cleanup.
register.action: DISABLE_DATA_FLOW before any record is changed

register.title: Rows present only in a replica
register.why: The primary no longer holds these rows, so the replica is the only copy left.
register.conflict: 12 of these carry direct identifiers and will be served to readers and reports.
register.action: DELETE_RECORD on the replica row, then re-check drift

register.title: Destructive operations that never reached SUCCESS
register.why: The run was reported as FAILED or PARTIAL and no later attempt on the same resource succeeded.
register.conflict: These stay in scope for every later audit and for any restore or sync that touches the same source.
register.action: Re-run the policy action, then verify the resulting state

register.title: Tombstones that still carry direct identifiers
register.why: A tombstone only needs the stable user reference.
register.conflict: Names, emails or phones left on a tombstone are directly identifying data with no purpose.

register.title: Superseded email, hash and phone values
register.why: The person replaced these values; 57 phone numbers were replaced over 12 months before the evidence window closed.
register.conflict: Older systems keyed to an old email or phone are missed when a request arrives under the current one.
register.action: Keep in the identity map for lookup, remove from live stores

register.title: Audit records with a defined retention end
register.why: Retention runs to 2031–2034; after that date the record is no longer required.
register.conflict: Keeping a record past its date turns a lawful retention into unnecessary storage of personal data.

register.title: Order records held for disputes and tax
register.why: Held under an active legal hold or tax rule; the register states a retain-until date.
register.conflict: The hold date has to be tracked: deleting early breaches the hold, keeping late breaches minimization.
register.action: RETAIN, review at the retain-until date
